transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

People at work are plotting against me and changing my routes on purpose, and no one believes me when I tell them it’s happening. They are secretly altering my routing projects behind my back to make me look incompetent, but my boss and my husband just brush it off as computer glitches or stress.
How has your mood been lately? Have you been feeling consistently down, sad, or hopeless, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

I’ve completely lost interest in everything I used to enjoy, like my choir, softball, and church. Most days after work I just lie on the couch in my uniform without showering, and I barely even speak to my husband because it feels like too much effort. I just don't have the energy to care about anything anymore.
Have there been times, lasting at least a couple of weeks, when your mood and energy felt completely normal, but you still believed people at work were plotting against you?

No, my mood and energy haven't felt normal at all during this time. Over the last couple of months, while the plotting at work has really taken over, I've also felt completely drained and flat. These feelings of low energy and the suspicions about my coworkers have been happening at the exact same time.
Before these past two months, have you ever had times in your life when you believed people were plotting against you, but your mood was otherwise completely fine and not depressed?

No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. The feeling that people are plotting against me only started as a nagging suspicion over the last year, and it's only gotten really intense in the last two months. Before this whole situation started a year ago, I never had these kinds of thoughts or issues at all.
During the past year when those nagging suspicions first started, before they got really intense two months ago, how was your mood?

Over the past year, my mood felt increasingly "off" and I felt completely burnt out. I started losing interest in things I used to love, like my choir and softball, and lacked any real energy or motivation. Most days after work, I would just lie on the couch because it felt like too much effort to do or feel anything at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a severe depressive episode characterized by profound anhedonia (loss of interest in choir, softball, and church), severe energy loss/fatigue (lying on the couch, unable to shower), and psychomotor retardation (finding speech to be too much effort). This is accompanied by persecutory delusions (believing coworkers are plotting against her and altering her routes). Because the psychotic symptoms have occurred exclusively during the active depressive state and there is no history of independent psychotic symptoms during periods of normal mood, a diagnosis of severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms (F32.3) is established, ruling out schizoaffective disorder (F25.1) and schizophrenia (F20.0).
